the_day: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet so its agents can pay for things with user approval, Google let US Gemini users connect Google Wallet, Anthropic set an IPO price range and was sued over its 'Mythos' name, and Meta's Muse agent can now place phone calls.

items.headline: Anthropic sets IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share
points: Anthropic set its share price range at $70 to $78, valuing it at up to $1.4 trillion, The Motley Fool reports.
Citybiz says the offering drew six times the available shares; Bloomberg reports share orders from China are being rebuffed.
On the roadshow, Dario Amodei called computing power the company's 'deepest business dilemma', Bloomberg reports.

items.headline: Anthropic publishes guidance on building stronger AI safety evaluations
points: Anthropic published a post on how to build stronger, more reliable safety evaluations for AI models.
Crypto Briefing says the post sets out 10 recommendations; FourWeekMBA highlights a case where one model's scores differed by 34 points.
items.for_you: Teams that test AI models for safety can compare their own evaluation methods against Anthropic's recommendations.

items.headline: Software company sues Anthropic over use of the 'Mythos' name
points: A software company has sued Anthropic for trademark infringement over its 'Mythos' model, Reuters reports.
Bloomberg Law reports the suit claims Anthropic stole the company's 'Mythos' brand.

items.headline: Gemini app can now use Google Wallet for spending insights
points: All Gemini app users in the US can now connect Google Wallet so answers draw on their spending habits.
Google presents it as a way to get personal finance insights inside the Gemini app.
items.for_you: If you use Gemini in the US, you can choose to link Google Wallet, which gives Gemini access to your spending data.

items.headline: Meta's Muse agent can now make phone calls for users
points: Meta's Muse AI agent can now place phone calls on a user's behalf, Dexerto and BigGo Finance report.
BigGo Finance says the feature is available to paid subscribers in the US.
items.for_you: If you pay for Muse in the US, you can ask it to make calls for you.

items.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so agents can make purchases
points: Agents in ChatGPT Work, Codex and dots can now complete purchases with user approval and existing card protections.
It works with Visa, Mastercard and American Express; CNBC reports it is available to Pro subscribers.
Help Net Security says agents pay without seeing card numbers; Trending Topics reports it is not available in the EU.
items.for_you: ChatGPT Pro subscribers outside the EU can let OpenAI's agents buy things for them, and each purchase needs their approval.
